source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter I, §7 Control of the Centre, Example 18

steps.title: The four centre squares
steps.source: The four squares, K 4 and Q 4 on each side respectively, are the centre squares, and control of these squares is called control of the centre. The control of the centre is of great importance.

narration.say: These four squares are the centre.
No violent attack can succeed without controlling at least two of them.

steps.title: A timid move
steps.source: A timid move. Black assumes a defensive attitude at once. On principle the move is wrong. In the openings, whenever possible, pieces should be moved in preference to Pawns.

narration.say: Pawn to e4, pawn to e5. Knight to f3.
Black plays d6. A timid move: in the opening, pieces should be moved in preference to pawns.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Take the offensive in the centre.

feedback.*: Strike in the centre with a pawn.

exercise.hint: The queen's pawn goes two squares.
exercise.success: 3. d4. White strives to control the centre. Black defends e5 with Nd7.

steps.title: A cramped position
steps.source: On principle the move is wrong, because it blocks the action of the Queen's Bishop, and instead of facilitating the action of Black's pieces, tends, on the contrary, to cramp them.

narration.say: The knight on d7 blocks Black's own bishop.
Bishop to c4. White threatens knight to g5, attacking f7.
Black must play h6, paying the penalty for his previous move.

steps.title: Deploy first, castle later
steps.source: It should be noticed that White does not Castle yet. The reason is that he wants to deploy his forces first.

narration.say: Bishop to e3, bishop to e7.
Queen to e2. White does not castle yet: he wants to deploy his forces first.
Black makes room for his queen with c6. Rook to d1, queen to c7.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Complete your development.

feedback.*: The king is still in the centre.

exercise.hint: Castle. Drag the king two squares to the right.
exercise.success: 9. O-O. White's position is unassailable: no weak spots, and every piece ready for action.

steps.title: What we learned
steps.source: The student should carefully study this example. It will show him that it is sometimes convenient to delay Castling.

narration.say: Control of the centre ensures the initiative.
Move pieces in preference to pawns, and do not block your own pieces.
And sometimes it is convenient to delay castling.
